To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current state of human genetics is that we have discovered many variants that explain little of the heritability and the future challenges we will face to discover more of the heritable variation are: 1) to discover the variants that are responsible for the missing heritability; 2) to understand their function; 3) to determine how they interact to produce the trait of interest and; 4) to translate the information from the genotype into the phenotype of interest.

1) the genetic variants that underlie complex traits are not the same as those that underlie monogenic traits, 2) the variants that underlie common traits are not the variants that underlies rare traits and 3) the variants that are found in one population are not necessarily the same as the variants that underly the same traits in other populations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic architecture of human complex traits, and how we can exploit this information to improve human health and well being.
the identification, characterisation, validation and exploitation of genetic variants that influence the risk of complex disease.

the identification of the genetic factors that influence the development of complex diseases and the use of that information to develop new approaches for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human complex trait genetics is still in its infancy and the lid of the genomics toolbox has not yet been lifted.
we have not yet found the right variants, or that we have not found them all, or that the methods we have are not yet sufficiently sensitive, or that we are not yet looking in the right places.
the human genome has been a very good investment, but it will be some time before we see the full return.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been successful in finding the variants but have been less successful in finding their biological relevance and the pathways they are involved with.
we are in a period of transition from the discovery phase of genetics to the application phase.
we are still in a very early phase of understanding human genetic variation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human genome is a very complex and dynamic system.
the human genome has a lot more information to give us than what we can currently detect.
the human genome is not as complex as it might seem, but the complexity is in the analysis and the interpretation.
